claims.text: V01: The ASA upheld an objection to Boohoo’s particular T-shirt product images on objectification and sexualisation grounds on 16 February 2022. The execution was seen in November 2021. Checked against primary source / local full-node evidence / acquisition receipt as applicable. Advertising Standards Authority. 2022. V02: The 6 April 2016 Gucci ruling distinguished two images and found one irresponsible in its presentation of thinness. It does not diagnose the model’s health. Checked against primary source / local full-node evidence / acquisition receipt as applicable. Advertising Standards Authority. 2016. V03: The revised 6 March 2024 Calvin Klein ruling reversed the objectification finding about FKA twigs while maintaining the objection to untargeted placement. Checked against primary source / local full-node evidence / acquisition receipt as applicable. Advertising Standards Authority. 2024. V04: ACM secured commitments from H&M and Decathlon in 2022 to adjust or stop insufficiently clear sustainability claims. Commitments must not be described as fines or criminal convictions. Checked against primary source / local full-node evidence / acquisition receipt as applicable. Netherlands Authority for Consumers and Markets. 2022. V05: Pantano’s study examines the Dolce & Gabbana chopsticks controversy through negative stereotype adoption and online diffusion. It supports a situated narrative and circulation analysis, not an adjudicated universal racial-discrimination finding. Checked against primary source / local full-node evidence / acquisition receipt as applicable. Pantano, Eleonora. 2021. When a luxury brand bursts. Journal of Business Research 123:117–125. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jbusres.2020.09.049
